line: In this town, every lie you tell
makes your shadow a little longer.
My name's Leo, and I thought I was a pretty honest kid.
Then on Monday, my mom asked if I'd brushed my teeth.
I said, yes.
My shadow grew one step.
Nobody noticed.
On Tuesday, I told my teacher the dog ate my homework.
We don't have a dog.
My shadow reached the door.
By Wednesday, I was lying about everything.
I said I liked my aunt's soup.
I said I'd already cleaned my room.
I said I scored a goal.
By Thursday, my shadow was so long it went down the whole street.
It tripped the mailman.
It scared the neighbor's cat.
And at night, it lay across the whole town like a black river.
People started asking questions.
Leo, why is your shadow in the bakery?
I said, that's not my shadow.
It grew another block.
Then came the worst part.
My little sister Mia got lost at the night market.
Everyone was looking for her.
And I couldn't find her, because my own shadow covered every street.
Everything was dark.
So I stood in the middle of the square, and I told the truth.
Mom, I never brushed my teeth.
Miss Rose, I don't have a dog.
Aunt Nora, your soup is terrible.
With every truth, my shadow shrank back.
Street by street, the lights came back.
And there, under a lamp, sat Mia, eating cotton candy.
She said, I wasn't lost.
I lied so you'd come find me.
And right behind her, her shadow was just starting to grow.
